title: Repentance, the Mustard Seed, and the Narrow Door

questions.question: Some present told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices. Jesus said, "Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered in this way?" What was His conclusion?
options: "No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish."
"Yes, for God exacts vengeance purely on the wicked."
"We cannot know the mind of God in random acts of terror."
"No, but they lacked the faith to foresee their death."
questions.correctAnswer: "No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish."
questions.explanation: Luke 13:3 (ESV): "No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish."

questions.question: What other tragic event did Jesus mention, asking if the eighteen people involved were worse offenders than all others in Jerusalem?
options: Those on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them
Those crushed in the stampede at the sheep gate
Those who drowned in the pool of Bethesda
Those who burned to death in the marketplace fire
questions.correctAnswer: Those on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them
questions.explanation: Luke 13:4 (ESV): "Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them..."

questions.question: In the Parable of the Barren Fig Tree, for how many years had the owner been looking for fruit on the tree without finding any?
options: Three years
Seven years
Forty years
One year
questions.explanation: Luke 13:7 (ESV): "And he said to the vinedresser, 'Look, for three years now I have come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and I find none. Cut it down.'"

questions.question: What did the vinedresser ask the owner to do with the barren fig tree?
options: "Sir, let it alone this year also, until I dig around it and put on manure."
"Cut it immediately, for it poisons the soil."
"Graft a new branch onto it and wait three more years."
"Sell the land, for it is cursed entirely."
questions.correctAnswer: "Sir, let it alone this year also, until I dig around it and put on manure."
questions.explanation: Luke 13:8 (ESV): "And he answered him, 'Sir, let it alone this year also, until I dig around it and put on manure.'"

questions.question: Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath. There was a woman who had a disabling spirit for how long? She was bent over and could not fully straighten herself.
options: Eighteen years
Twelve years
Since birth
Ten months
questions.explanation: Luke 13:11 (ESV): "And behold, there was a woman who had had a disabling spirit for eighteen years. She was bent over and could not fully straighten herself."

questions.question: Why was the ruler of the synagogue indignant when Jesus healed the woman?
options: Because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath
Because the woman was a known sinner in the village
Because Jesus did not pay the synagogue tax after
Because the woman screamed loudly and disrupted prayer
questions.correctAnswer: Because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath
questions.explanation: Luke 13:14 (ESV): "But the ruler of the synagogue, indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, said to the people, 'There are six days in which work ought to be done...'"

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to the ruler of the synagogue calling him a hypocrite?
options: "Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or his donkey from the manger and lead it away to water it?"
"And who untied the manna for you on the Sabbath in the desert?"
"Your laws are heavy burdens that weigh on the poor."
"The son of man is Lord even of your precious synagogue."
questions.correctAnswer: "Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or his donkey from the manger and lead it away to water it?"
questions.explanation: Luke 13:15 (ESV): "Then the Lord answered him, 'You hypocrites! Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or his donkey from the manger and lead it away to water it?'"

questions.question: What does Jesus compare the kingdom of God to, involving a garden?
options: A grain of mustard seed that a man took and sowed in his garden, and it grew and became a tree
A fig tree planted by a river that bears twelve kinds of fruit
An olive branch that spreads across a violent storm
A vineyard protected by a tall stone wall
questions.correctAnswer: A grain of mustard seed that a man took and sowed in his garden, and it grew and became a tree
questions.explanation: Luke 13:19 (ESV): "It is like a grain of mustard seed that a man took and sowed in his garden, and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the air made nests in its branches."

questions.question: What does Jesus compare the kingdom of God to, involving baking?
options: Leaven that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until it was all leavened
The firstfruits of the finest wheat harvest baked in stone
Salt that gives flavor to the daily bread of the poor
Manna melting before the full sun rises
questions.correctAnswer: Leaven that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until it was all leavened
questions.explanation: Luke 13:20-21 (ESV): "It is like leaven that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until it was all leavened."

questions.question: Someone asked Jesus, "Lord, will those who are saved be few?" What did Jesus command them to strive entirely to do?
options: "Strive to enter through the narrow door. For many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able."
"Keep all the commandments perfectly from your youth."
"Give all your money to the temple treasury today."
"Wash yourselves seven times in the Jordan river."
questions.correctAnswer: "Strive to enter through the narrow door. For many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able."
questions.explanation: Luke 13:24 (ESV): "Strive to enter through the narrow door. For many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able."

questions.question: When the master of the house has locked the door and people begin to knock saying "Lord, open to us," what will he answer?
options: "I do not know where you come from."
"You are late for the wedding feast."
"Your sins have kept you outside the walls."
"Only those bearing gifts may enter tonight."
questions.correctAnswer: "I do not know where you come from."
questions.explanation: Luke 13:25 (ESV): "he will answer you, 'I do not know where you come from.'"

questions.question: What will those outside say to try to convince the master to let them in, and what will the master finally command them?
options: "We ate and drank in your presence... 'Depart from me, all you workers of evil!'"
"We gave half our wealth away... 'You did it for pride!'"
"We healed the sick in your town... 'I never knew your works.'"
"We carried your cross... 'You did not suffer enough.'"
questions.correctAnswer: "We ate and drank in your presence... 'Depart from me, all you workers of evil!'"
questions.explanation: Luke 13:26-27 (ESV): "Then you will begin to say, 'We ate and drank in your presence...' But he will say, 'I tell you, I do not know where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of evil!'"

questions.question: Some Pharisees warned Jesus to "Get away from here, for Herod wants to kill you." What animal did Jesus call Herod?
options: That fox
That serpent
That roaring lion
That unclean dog
questions.explanation: Luke 13:32 (ESV): "And he said to them, 'Go and tell that fox, "Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I finish my course."'"

questions.question: Jesus laments over Jerusalem: "O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to it! How often would I have gathered your children together as..."?
options: "...a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!"
"...a shepherd gathers his flock before the storm!"
"...a mother gathers her sons from a burning house!"
"...a farmer gathers wheat into his barn!"
questions.correctAnswer: "...a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!"
questions.explanation: Luke 13:34 (ESV): "How often would I have gathered your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!"

questions.question: What does Jesus say Jerusalem will not see Him again until they say?
options: "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!"
"You alone are the Holy One of Israel!"
"Forgive us our trespasses against the Son!"
"The Kingdom has returned to the house of David!"
questions.correctAnswer: "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!"
questions.explanation: Luke 13:35 (ESV): "And I tell you, you will not see me until you say, 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!'"

key_verse_text: "Strive to enter through the narrow door. For many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able."
